title: Check yourself: What a hook decides, and what it cannot undo

questions.stem: A PreToolUse hook is meant to rewrite a command before it runs. It returns the new input in a field next to `hookSpecificOutput`, and the original command runs unchanged. What is the cause?

options.text: The value is honoured only when nested in the answer structure
options.says: The answer is read only from its documented place.

options.text: A rewrite takes effect only if the hook answers with a deferral
options.says: Ruled out because a deferral discards the change: "the input is dropped".

options.text: Commands can be rewritten only by a hook that runs as a separate program
options.says: Ruled out because callback hooks may change input too: "Pair `updatedInput` with `permissionDecision: 'allow'` to auto-approve the modified input".

options.text: The rewrite was applied, then undone by the session's permission mode
options.says: Ruled out because nothing undoes a change that is applied: "the modified input still applies and flows through the normal permission evaluation".

questions.stem: A team adds a hook with the matcher `src/payments/*` to review every write under that folder. The hook never fires. What is the best fix?

options.text: Switch the matcher to a regular expression that also lists every file in the folder
options.says: Ruled out because "Matchers only match tool names, not file paths or other arguments."

options.text: Raise the timeout of the hook
options.says: Ruled out because the timeout bounds the callback and has nothing to do with matching: "Each callback runs with a timeout in seconds".

options.text: Attach it to the file-editing tools and test the path inside the callback
options.says: A matcher sees only the name of the tool, so the path is read from the input.

options.text: Move the hook to the PostToolUse event, which evaluates paths after the write
options.says: Ruled out because the post event comes after the tool and cannot change what a matcher sees: "the tool already ran".
